info.title: API specification for Glomo
info.description:
The Glomo API follows REST architecture, utilizing resource-oriented URLs for clarity. It handles form-encoded request bodies, delivers responses in JSON format, and operates with standard HTTP methods, authentication, and response codes.

You can download the complete API collection by using the download options on the right.

tags.name: balance_conversions
tags.description: Balance Conversion resource represents the details of the balance conversion. The balance conversion is the conversion of the balance from one supported currency to another supported currency.

tags.name: payment_link
tags.description: A payment link is a shareable URL that will take your customers to a Glomo-hosted payment page. The payment page can only be accessed by your customer after the completion of 1FA via their email.

tags.name: Customer
tags.description: This resource represents a customer of your business. The customer can be an individual or a business from whom you will receive payments.

tags.name: Document
tags.description: Document resource represents the documents details uploaded. This document is used in payin, payout, etc.

tags.name: Payment
tags.description: This resource represents a payment attempt made by your customer. The payment can either be successfully completed or failed, depending on various factors.

tags.name: Refund
tags.description: This resource represents a refund transaction from your Glomo account to your customer. You can retrieve it to see the details of the refund transaction.

tags.name: Payout
tags.description: This resource represents the disbursement transactions from your Glomo account to your beneficiaries.

tags.name: Balance
tags.description: This resource represents your Glomo balance. You can retrieve it to see the current balance on your Glomo account in all currencies enabled for your account.

tags.name: bank_account_validation
tags.description: Bank Account Validation resource represents the validation details of a bank account.

tags.name: Beneficiary
tags.description: This resource represents a payee of a payout initiated by your business. The beneficiary can be an individual or a business to whom you will send funds.

tags.name: Price
tags.description: This resource represents the pricing details of the payin or payout. The pricing details include the fees and the pricing type

tags.name: Withdrawal
tags.description: **[DEPRECATED]** This resource represents the withdrawal transaction from your Glomo account to your withdrawal account.

tags.name: withdrawal_account
tags.description: This resource represents the withdrawal account details. The withdrawal account is the bank account where the withdrawal amount will be credited.

tags.name: Orders
tags.description: This resource represents the order details. The order is the request to receive payment from your customer.

tags.name: Subscription
tags.description: This resource represents a recurring billing agreement for a customer. Subscriptions allow businesses to automatically charge customers on a regular schedule according to a defined billing plan.

tags.name: Webhook
tags.description: This resource represents the webhook details. The webhook is the endpoint where the webhook events will be sent.

tags.name: Settlement
tags.description: This resource represents the settlement details. The settlement is the process of transferring funds from your Glomo account to your bank account.

tags.name: virtual_account
tags.description: This resource represents virtual account details. A virtual account is a unique account number provisioned for a customer, allowing payments to be received and transactions to be tracked against that customer.

tags.name: platform
tags.description: This resource provides platform functionality that enables platforms to onboard merchants onto Glomo, with each merchant having their own dedicated Virtual Accounts (VA).

tags.name: internal_transfer
tags.description:
This resource represents internal fund movements between merchant accounts within the platform–partner model. Internal transfers enable seamless fund movement between merchants who operate under the same platform account. Internal transfers are restricted to accounts linked under the same platform hierarchy. The following transfer directions are supported:
| Transfer Type                  | Description                                                                    |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **P → C**                      | From a **Platform** (P) account to one of its **Child** (C) merchant accounts. |
| **C → P**                      | From a **Child** (C) merchant account back to its **Platform** (P) account.    |
| **C → C (same P)**             | Between **Child** (C) accounts under the same **Platform** (P). |

get.description: Retrieves available balances for all currencies.

post.description: Converts balance from one currency to another. In the API you can either send `target_amount` or `source_amount` and the API will calculate the other amount for you.

source_currency.description: The currency code in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. Supported currencies: USD,EUR and GBP.

target_currency.description: The currency code in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. Supported currencies: USD,EUR and GBP.

source_amount.description: The amount you want to convert. A positive integer representing the smallest currency unit.  For example, if the amount is $299.00, then pass 29900 in this field.  In the case of three decimal currencies, such as KWD, BHD and OMR, to represent an amount of 295.991, pass the value as 295990.  And in the case of zero decimal currencies such as JPY, for amount ￥295, pass the value as 295. ``` Only one of `source_amount` or `target_amount` can be sent. ```

source_currency.description: The currency code in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. Supported currencies: USD,EUR and GBP.

target_currency.description: The currency code in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. Supported currencies: USD,EUR and GBP.

target_amount.description: The amount you want to receive. A positive integer representing the smallest currency unit.  For example, if the amount is $299.00, then pass 29900 in this field.  In the case of three decimal currencies, such as KWD, BHD and OMR, to represent an amount of 295.991, pass the value as 295990.  And in the case of zero decimal currencies such as JPY, for amount ￥295, pass the value as 295. ``` Only one of `source_amount` or `target_amount` can be sent. ```

message.description: Error message.
message.example: You can only send source_amount or target_amount, not both.

error.description:
The specific validation error message indicating why the mock funds available operation failed.

**Possible Error Messages:**

- **Payment Status Error:** `Payment must be in success status`
- **Gateway Error:** `Payment must be from LRS gateway`
- **Settlement Error:** `Payment must not have direct settlement enabled`
- **Transaction Error:** `No transaction found for payment`
- **Funds Already Available:** `Transaction already has funds available`

transfer_amount.description: The amount transferred in cents. For example, 1000 cents is 10.00.

transfer_currency.description: The currency in which the transfer was made. The currency code is in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format.

reference.description: The reference identifier provided for the transfer.

fees.description: The fees associated with the internal transfer.

txn_fee.description: The transaction fee charged for the internal transfer.

fx_fee.description: The foreign exchange fee charged for the internal transfer.

error_code.description: The error code if the internal transfer failed, null otherwise.

error_description.description: The error description if the internal transfer failed, null otherwise.

created_at.description: The creation timestamp of the internal transfer.

updated_at.description: The last update timestamp of the internal transfer.

BeforeParam.name: before
BeforeParam.description: [ISO-8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) timestamp in UTC to filter resources created before this time. Use this to avoid `Page drift` issue. See [Pagination parameters](\./pagination#pagination-parameters) for more details.

AfterParam.name: after
AfterParam.description: [ISO-8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) timestamp in UTC to filter resources created after this time. Use this to avoid `Page drift` issue. See [Pagination parameters](\./pagination#pagination-parameters) for more details.

PerPageParam.name: per_page
PerPageParam.description: Number of resources per page. Should be between 1 and 100.

PageParam.name: page
PageParam.description: Page number for pagination. Starts from 1. Get the next page number from the `next` field in the response.
